newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee lower after NY fall Monday.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee lower after NY fall Monday.

text.p: LIFFE coffee moved lower during Tuesday morning, following New York's fall Monday.
Traders said the move was what they had been expecting, on the basis of New York. "It's just as expected. There's nothing really featuring," one said.
By the midday break, benchmark July was down $47 at $2,053 on volume of 1,232 lots of a total 2,331.
"I wouldn't say it has run out of steam at the moment," one said. "People are getting a bit euphoric about the rise, which is dangerous," he said.
"It's still a question of waiting for New York, which still seems to have a bit of fire in it," he said.
"The situation in robustas is that it does not face a severe supply shortage," he said.
CSCE coffee futures pulled back sharply Monday, led by a massive slide in the May contract as operators rushed to liquidate long positions ahead of the spot contract's expiry at noon EDT.
Before the LIFFE market opened, Susan Rigg, analyst at Chart Analysis, said July looked "overstretched."

The International Coffee Organization (ICO) said on Monday that spiralling coffee markets face a risk of big falls in prices if investment funds liquidate their massive positions built over the past few months.
ICO members continue their week long talks in London on Tuesday.
